nonblocking_findings: The hoist is done correctly. `$note-anchor-leaves` is now built once per emit-leaves call (reledmac.xslt:2146-2148), next to `$head-divs`. It uses the same predicate as the head-note skip branch (2585-2586) and is tunnelled only from the `otherwise` emit branch (2617-2622). So no leaf the stream skips can act as a neighbour, and every leaf the stream prints is in the sequence. One cost remains: f:note-neighbor still scans `$leaves` linearly to find each note's position (4032-4033), and it runs once for the backward lookup plus once per step of f:adjacent-notes. That makes the cost O(notes × leaves) per stream rather than O(leaves²). It is acceptable, but if build time matters, a map from note id to position would remove it.

f:same-note-location (4046-4056) is symmetric. The backward lookup (4081-4083) and the forward lookup (4062-4064) apply the same rule, so a group's first note and the notes it suppresses still agree: no mark is lost or printed twice. It also correctly fixes the defect you found. A hoisted heading note is emitted through the heading template's `$notes`, where no stream sequence is tunnelled, so it falls back to XML siblings and used to combine with an explicitly targeted body note in the same div. That is now blocked in both directions.

Possible narrow regression (safe direction). f:head-note-div is structural (2892-2904): it does not depend on the stream. Take a head note whose heading is not an f:head in the current stream. It is not in `$head-divs`, so it stays in the flow (the 'anything else keeps its place' case at 2126-2127). It still has a non-empty head-note-div, though, so f:same-note-location now refuses to group it with a plain body note that prints at the same point. Before this round they would have combined. The result is two overlapping zero-width marks, not a lost mark. This is probably rare, and the byte-identical preview TeX suggests it does not happen there, but no test covers it. A tighter condition would compare locations only when both notes are actually hoisted, i.e. their div is in `$head-divs`. That set is not visible inside the function, so a tunnel or parameter would be needed.

Heading-group fallback is still uneven, as before. Notes on a division (siblings of tei:head) and notes inside tei:head are emitted together, sorted, after the title. They are not XML siblings of each other, though, so the sibling fallback gives them separate marks at the same point. Notes of the same kind (two division notes or two notes inside the head) do still group. This is the nested fallback you accepted earlier. Grouping by position in `$notes` inside the heading template would close it.

The silent boundary leaves from the previous review are unchanged and stay conservative: unrendered or parsha.* milestones, and echoed rubrics, still split a group. There is still no look-through, as agreed.

Tests: the parallel-stream test confirms two separate pairs with each note's text printed once. It checks the serials as a multiset, not which stream each pair is in, but within-stream grouping plus a paragraph boundary in each column makes cross-stream pairing impossible here. The hoisted-heading test covers the sibling defect directly. Not covered: an in-flow, non-hoisted head note next to a body note (see above); an anchor with content acting as a boundary; and a mixed leaf-and-nested case.

The test log reports 375 tests OK. The 'XTDE0050 No value supplied for required parameter typography-preamble' line is stderr from what looks like a test that expects an error, since the run still passes. It is not a failure, but someone should confirm it is expected noise and not a test that quietly passes on an error path.
I did not open or verify note-fix-hardened-tex-proof.json or the claim that the preview TeX is byte-identical. This review is of the code and tests only.
verdict: Approve. The requested hardening is in place: the per-leaf filter is computed once per stream, parallel-stream and hoisted-heading regression tests exist, and the sibling defect found while hardening (a hoisted heading note combining with an explicitly targeted body note, which then printed its own mark again) is fixed symmetrically by f:same-note-location. Every apparatus entry still emits its own \edtext, \Bfootnote/\Bendnote, \OSFootnotemark and content. Only the text of the interlinear mark changes. The one possible regression goes the safe way: a head note left in the flow whose heading is not in this stream no longer combines with a plain body neighbour, which can overlap two marks but never loses one. That and the remaining coverage gaps are not blocking. This review does not cover the rendered page: the PDF206 visual check, including that 128 and 129 print as one comma-separated mark, is still a separate gate.
